title: Caption Distillation for ReVision-Style Text-Only MLLM Pretraining: An Empirical Study

contributions.purpose: Tests whether content-aware sentence selection can mitigate the Long-Caption Paradox (longer captions hurting performance) in ReVision-style text-only MLLM pretraining.
contributions.mechanism: The first systematic controlled micro-scale experiment comparing three conditions: (A) original long captions, (B) random length-matched selection, and (C) CLIP-scored caption distillation selecting visually-relevant sentences by image-text similarity.
contributions.evaluation: The hypothesis is not supported: CLIP-scored distillation (51.88% mean accuracy) underperforms long captions (53.31%) by 1.43 percentage points, though content-aware selection beats random selection (49.90%) by 1.98 points.
contributions.source_quote: The first systematic study of caption distillation for ReVision-style text-only MLLM pretraining, providing a rigorous test of whether content-aware sentence selection can mitigate the Long-Caption Paradox.

contributions.purpose: Explains mechanistically why sentence-level caption filtering fails despite preserving visually relevant content.
contributions.mechanism: Analysis of what information sentence-level filtering discards, measured via object-presence benchmarks.
contributions.evaluation: Sentence-level filtering inevitably loses object-presence mentions, evidenced by POPE recall dropping from 98% to 88%.
contributions.source_quote: A negative result with mechanistic explanation: sentence-level filtering inevitably loses object-presence mentions, as evidenced by POPE recall dropping from 98% to 88%.

contributions.purpose: Directs future work toward an approach that could preserve information the filtering approach loses.
contributions.mechanism: Derives from the failure analysis the suggestion that caption condensation (rewriting to preserve information in fewer words) may succeed where sentence filtering fails.
contributions.evaluation: Presented as an actionable insight derived from the negative result, not itself experimentally validated on pages 1-2.
contributions.source_quote: An actionable insight for future work: caption condensation (rewriting to preserve information in fewer words) may succeed where filtering fails.

self_declared_provenance.quote: This paradox is particularly pronounced in ReVision-style text-only pretraining (Yu et al., 2026), which enables MLLM training without paired images by exploiting the modality gap in contrastive embedding spaces.

We hypothesize that CLIP-scored caption distillation—selecting the most visually-relevant sentences from long captions based on image-text similarity—could mitigate this paradox by preserving information density while reducing length.
